issues.description: fieldsWriter throws UnsupportedOperationException instead of encoding read-only-ness in the type system.
issues.detail: All three reviewers flag this as the central design flaw. KnnVectorsFormat.fieldsWriter's contract is to return a writer; the legacy formats now throw at runtime, breaking substitutability and forcing callers to know a hidden rule. Introduce a ReadOnlyKnnVectorsFormat supertype (or sealed variant) so the read-only invariant is compiler-enforced rather than a runtime trap.

issues.description: DIRECT_MONOTONIC_BLOCK_SHIFT constant duplicated rather than imported from its canonical source.
issues.detail: Previously imported from Lucene99FlatVectorsFormat, the constant is now redeclared on Lucene99ScalarQuantizedVectorsFormat with no compiler-enforced link to the original. Two sources of truth for the same on-disk parameter invites invariant drift. Either keep importing the canonical value, move it to a shared spec class, or document why the legacy copy is intentionally frozen.

issues.description: OffHeapQuantizedByteVectorValues remains public abstract but fields demoted from protected to package-private.
issues.detail: The class is still public abstract with a public nested subclass, yet shared fields lost protected access. External subclasses the public abstraction implicitly invited can no longer be written. Either make the class package-private to seal the hierarchy, or restore protected fields to match the public extension contract.

issues.description: Constructor still accepts numMergeWorkers and mergeExec that the read-only format silently discards.
issues.detail: The fields backing these parameters were removed but the constructor signature retains them and even validates them. Callers pass data that has no effect, making the constructor signature lie about behavior. Drop the dead parameters or document them as source-compatibility shims only.

issues.description: Backward_codecs module still imports core lucene99 internals, leaving the boundary porous.
issues.detail: The moved classes import org.apache.lucene.codecs.lucene99.Lucene99HnswVectorsFormat/Reader and Lucene99FlatVectorsFormat. The backward_codecs module is meant to seal legacy code; reaching back into current core means future changes there can silently break legacy contracts. Either copy needed pieces into backward_codecs or expose a stable shared interface.

issues.description: RW test scaffolds duplicate format wiring instead of parameterizing one class, and V1 hardcodes default graph params.
issues.detail: Lucene99RWV0 and Lucene99RWV1 are near-identical except for which writer they call — the inheritance-as-switch antipattern. Worse, the V1 constructor accepts maxConn/beamWidth but the writer is built with DEFAULT_MAX_CONN/DEFAULT_BEAM_WIDTH, silently ignoring caller input. Collapse to one parameterized RW format and pass the actual graph params through.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the relocation to backward_codecs is directionally correct but the contract work is incomplete. The central flaw is that read-only-ness is encoded as a runtime UnsupportedOperationException on fieldsWriter rather than as a type (e.g., a ReadOnlyKnnVectorsFormat supertype), violating substitutability and forcing hidden caller rules. Secondary issues cluster around duplicated state and inconsistent access: DIRECT_MONOTONIC_BLOCK_SHIFT redeclared instead of imported, OffHeapQuantizedByteVectorValues left public-abstract while its fields became package-private, and constructors retaining dead merge-executor parameters. The fix path is consistent across reviewers: introduce a read-only supertype, deduplicate the constant, reconcile class visibility with its extension contract, and tighten the module boundary.
